module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The Bing-Borsuk Conjecture

The Bing-Borsuk conjecture states that every $n$-dimensional homogeneous absolute neighborhood
retract is a topological $n$-manifold.

The conjecture has been verified in dimensions $1$ and $2$ but remains open in higher dimensions.
A notable consequence is that if the $3$-dimensional case is true, it implies the Poincaré
conjecture.

*References:*
 - [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing%E2%80%93Borsuk_conjecture)
 - [HR2008] Halverson, Denise M., and Dušan Repovš. "The Bing-Borsuk and the Busemann
   conjectures." Mathematical Communications 13.2 (2008): 163-184.
   https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.0886
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace BingBorsuk

open scoped Manifold
open TopologicalSpace

/--
The Bing-Borsuk Conjecture: every $n$-dimensional homogeneous absolute neighborhood retract
is a topological $n$-manifold. A topological space $X$ is an $n$-dimensional manifold
when `T2Space X ∧ Nonempty (ChartedSpace (Fin n → ℝ) X)`. The hypothesis `[MetrizableSpace X]`
implies `T2Space X` so this does not appear in the conclusion.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 54 57]
theorem bing_borsuk_conjecture : ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [MetrizableSpace X] [HomogeneousSpace X] [IsAbsoluteNeighborhoodRetract X],
    HasLebesgueCoveringDimensionEq X n → Nonempty (ChartedSpace (Fin n → ℝ) X) := by
  sorry

end BingBorsuk

findings.description: The hypothesis `IsAbsoluteNeighborhoodRetract X` uses retractions for closed embeddings into every `NormalSpace Y` (the helper's line 36), whereas both cited sources define ANRs using metric ambient spaces. This distinction is substantive: Hanner's Theorem 17.1(c) says that a metrizable ANR is an ANR for normal spaces exactly when it is separable and completely metrizable. Thus the Lean hypothesis implicitly restricts the conjecture to Polish ANRs. I could not establish that complete metrizability follows from the source's finite-dimensionality and homogeneity hypotheses. This is marked questionable rather than a definite misformalization because the literature also uses the locally compact ENR formulation, and equivalence of the complete conjecture formulations needs clarification.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia, Definitions, explicitly quantifies over embeddings into a metric space: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing%E2%80%93Borsuk_conjecture. Halverson–Repovš, https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.0886, §2 likewise defines ANR using metric ambient spaces, and Conjecture 3.1 states that every n-dimensional homogeneous ANR is an n-manifold without adding complete metrizability. Its introduction instead uses ENRs. For the distinction between ambient categories, see Hanner, 'Retraction and extension of mappings of metric and nonmetric spaces', Arkiv för Matematik 2 (1952), §14 and Theorem 17.1(c), p. 339.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify which formulation is intended. To follow the metric-ANR definition in the cited sources, use an ANR predicate quantifying over `[MetrizableSpace Y]`, and explicitly state the intended separability convention. If the locally compact ENR formulation is intended, state its local compactness and separability hypotheses and document the equivalence. Alternatively, retain the current statement with a reference establishing that restricting to completely metrizable ANRs is equivalent for this conjecture.

reformulations.difference: The conclusion supplies only `Nonempty (ChartedSpace (Fin n → ℝ) X)`, without explicit Hausdorffness or separability, while Halverson–Repovš defines an n-manifold as a separable metric space with Euclidean neighborhoods.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under the CURRENT hypotheses, metrizability gives Hausdorffness, and the normal-space ANR property gives separability by Hanner's Theorem 17.1(c). A charted-space structure supplies homeomorphisms between open subsets of X and ℝⁿ; shrinking a chart target to an open ball gives a neighborhood homeomorphic to ℝⁿ. Conversely, Euclidean neighborhoods supply an atlas. Hence no separate missing-separability defect occurs in the conclusion. This does not resolve the input-class restriction identified in the finding.

reformulations.difference: The ANR helper represents a neighborhood retraction using a total function `r : Y → X` with `ContinuousOn r U`, rather than a continuous function with domain the subtype U.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For nonempty X, restrict a total map to U in one direction and extend a map on U by an arbitrary point of X outside U in the other. The retraction identity is preserved because the embedded image lies in U. This equivalence was proved in `total_retraction_iff_subtype` in the scratch file. The current ANR predicate excludes empty X, but this does not change the conjecture's content at the empty space, which admits an empty atlas in every dimension.

sources_consulted: Halverson–Repovš, 'The Bing-Borsuk and the Busemann Conjectures', arXiv:0811.0886v2; LaTeX source, especially §§1–3 and 7: https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.0886

Hanner, 'Retraction and extension of mappings of metric and nonmetric spaces', Arkiv för Matematik 2 (1952), 315–360, especially §§2, 14 and 17: https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/116/6886-11512_2007_Article_BF02591501.pdf
Mardešić, 'Absolute Neighborhood Retracts and Shape Theory', History of Topology (1999), especially pp. 241–247: https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/mardesic.pdf
Ancel–Bellamy, 'On homogeneous locally conical spaces', arXiv:1607.00103, introduction and ENR formulation: https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.00103
could_not_verify: BingBorsuk.bing_borsuk_conjecture: full equivalence between the stated normal-space-ANR formulation and the cited metric-ANR/ENR formulations remains unsettled in this review. In particular, I did not establish that the implicit complete-metrizability restriction is redundant for all finite-dimensional homogeneous metric ANRs.
review.notes: Checked the sole theorem and all three repository-specific predicates. Homogeneity, finite-cover refinements, multiplicity n+1, exact dimension, and quantifier scope match their intended meanings. No answer slot or formal-proof claim is present, and the cited sources support the open status. `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` compiled without errors: it checks Hausdorffness/normality from metrizability, satisfiable singleton hypotheses and dimension zero, exclusion of positive singleton dimensions, empty-space behavior, and the retraction-domain equivalence. The target file was verified byte-for-byte against the specified commit; review files were written only under `/workspace/review/`.
